text:
olga: Quick experiment proposal — tune batch merge_delay from 1.5ms -> 0.7ms and add Poisson jitter (λ=0.6) to reduce synchronous flushes. Also lower per-route token_budget target on heavy routes to 32 tokens. Main risks: kernel-selection thrash + KV cache churn. Thoughts?

sam: SGTM as a canary, want explicit metrics + rollback criteria before we flip.

maya: +1. add kernel selection churn, kv_hit_ratio, and eviction rate to the watchlist.

josh: propose rollout plan: 10% traffic to canary on ded-pool-a. Command: ```kubectl -n inference set image deploy/runner runtime=redwood/runtime:canary-merge0.7``` then toggle routing weight.

ci-bot: canary deploy started at 2026-03-18T16:30:12Z :rocket:

kevin: heads up — smaller merge delay can shrink batch sizes which may increase kernel switches. Watch GPU util variance and kernel_selection_count.

olga: noted. explicit metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, mean batch_size, batch_size histogram, kernel_selection_count, kernel_context_switches, kv_hit_ratio, evictions_per_sec, effective_batched_tokens, tail_sla_violations.

sam: add kv_cache_lookup_latency and kv_miss_penalty_ms too.

maya: run two jitter modes in parallel if we can: Poisson vs Uniform so we can compare distribution effects. Different RNG seeds.

josh: can do. I'll start two canaries: ```kubectl -n inference set image deploy/runner runtime=redwood/runtime:canary-merge0.7-poisson``` and ```...:canary-merge0.7-uniform``` and split 5%/5%.

ci-bot: canaries healthy after 2m :white_check_mark:

josh: preliminary 10min snapshot: p99 latency +8ms, avg latency -6%, mean batch_size -12%, kv_hit_ratio -1.5%. Kernel_selection_count up ~22%.

kevin: kv_hit_ratio drop + kernel_selection bump = higher eviction churn. That could hurt certain long-context flows.

olga: ok let's try targeted mitigation: for routes with high kv dependency (/long-chat, /session-restore) bump token_budget -> 48 and increase kv TTL by 20%. Re-run Poisson canary for 30m.

sam: rollback criteria: increase p99 > +15ms OR kv_hit_ratio drop > 5% OR evictions/sec increase > 50% over baseline -> automatic rollback.

maya: logging note: tag traces with `experiment=merge0.7_poisson` and `jitter=poisson` so queries are filterable. Also dump kernel profile on one pod: `/scripts/profiler dump --pid=$(pgrep runtime) | gzip > /tmp/kernel-prof.gz`

josh: added profiling job and captured a 60s kernel trace. uploading to perf-dashboard.

ci-bot: perf job finished, artifacts at https://artifacts.redwood.internal/perf/1765432100/merge0.7_poisson.tar.gz

kevin: quick interpretation from profile: more frequent short-lived kernels (attention variant switching) and increased memcpy ops. That matches the kernel thrash hypothesis.

olga: thanks. Action items: 1) run widened token_budget for kv-heavy routes, 2) test uniform jitter variant, 3) collect 2h aggregated metrics and compare cost/token. I'll post a summary to perf-dashboard and follow up with recommended default merge_delay.

sam: sounds good. If widened token_budget fixes evictions, we can consider lowering merge_delay by 30-50% on lower-sensitivity routes.

maya: also suggest an automated per-route advisor: if kv_hit_ratio falls below threshold, fall back to larger token_budget.

olga: adding that to roadmap. Thanks all — will update when 2h run completes.
